Posted January 19, 2000

(MarijuanaNews note: The Orange County Weekly was right when it predicted that arresting Steve Kubby was the worst mistake the narks could make.)


See
After Interview With Steve Kubby, Orange County Weekly Says
Arresting Him " May Have Been Prop 215 Opponents' Worst Mistake "

From THE AMERICAN MEDICAL MARIJUANA ASSOCIATION
Monarch Bay Plaza, Box 375, Dana Point, Ca 92629
1/19/00

ASSERTING AND DEFENDING OUR MEDICAL RIGHTS by Steve Kubby

It's been exactly a year now since my wife and I were raided, robbed and arrested by twenty overweight deputies decked out in combat gear and laser-guided weapons. At the time, we believed we were patriotically asserting new medical rights that we had legally won at the ballot box.


Now, a year later, having survived a frightening assault on our lives, our home, our possessions and our family, we have learned that our criminal justice system is broken.

Apparently, asserting our lawful rights is no longer tolerated by law enforcement, if marijuana is involved:

--Just ask Marvin Chavez, who will spend today in prison, working in the cold, suffering great pain, because he is no longer allowed to use his back brace.
See
" The state prison officials are denying me the use of cannabis as my medication. "
A New Letter From Medical Marijuana Prisoner Marvin Chavez
--Or ask Todd McCormick, who will spend the next two years in painful incarceration, deprived of medicine, waiting for a chance to appeal his illegal gardening project.
--Or ask Peter McWilliams, who was foolish enough to believe the voter ballot guide, which said: " This initiative allows unlimited quantities of marijuana to be grown anywhere . . . without any regulation or restrictions. "
See
Buckley Denounces Prosecution of McCormick and McWilliams In Strongest Terms Yet.
" On the eve of the trial Judge King decided, so to speak, to eliminate the Bill of Rights. "
--Or ask David Herrick, who served with distinction as a deputy sheriff for 15 years, was disabled, and then tried to help others in pain by volunteering his time at a medical marijuana dispensary. Herrick was arrested, convicted, and sent to prison for something that is not supposed to be a crime under the Compassionate Use Act. Another judge finally agreed and released Herrick as a victim of malicious prosecution. Instead of receiving an apology for this outrage, Herrick was forced to wait months to see if he would be recharged.
See
California Court Overturns Conviction Of Medical Marijuana Activist David Herrick
– Prosecutorial Misconduct Cited. No Ruling On Medical Marijuana
When efforts to assert rights granted to us by a vote of the People are met with such unlawful behavior by the police and when elected official are afraid to take any meaningful actions against rogue police, then we can only conclude that our criminal justice system has been badly corrupted and is in a failure mode.

Our great American system of justice, once based upon tolerance, is now based upon an ideology of Zero Tolerance. Those who once bravely defended us, have been replaced by cowardly narcotics agents who spy on sick people by peeking through windows and collecting their garbage. Freedom is out; fear is in.

Our goal within the medical marijuana community is not to legalize marijuana, but to assert and secure rights already granted by the People.

Medical marijuana patients, doctors and activists have no interest in protests or " smoke-ins, " but we have an intense interest in activities that " smoke-out " rogue cops and corrupt officials and hold them accountable for their criminal behavior. We have just begun our campaign to smoke-out those who hide behind their offices to illegally threaten our civil and medical rights. We intend to expose corrupt sheriffs and predatory district
attorneys for what they really are -- a menace to society.

Our biggest weapon is the Internet, where we can transmit information that targets official lies and deception. Honest officials will hear and heed us. Corrupt officials will stand out in sharp relief. The challenge ahead is to carefully document the crimes committed by rogue cops and corrupt officials now, so that they can be held publicly accountable in the future.

Thus far, our efforts have been directed towards testing elected officials in ways that will tell us who is honest and who is not. Those public officials and law enforcement who continue to ignore us, will only hurt their credibility and help create a paper trail for later civil rights actions, under a more enlightened administration.

In the meantime, we are downloading large amounts of key information to law enforcement, elected officials and media, in order to serve public notice on them and to document the crimes of those who willfully and maliciously violate patients' civil and medical rights.

Asserting our lawful rights may not be easy, but rights not asserted or defended are soon lost. The fight for medical rights has only just begun.

THE AMERICAN MEDICAL MARIJUANA ASSOCIATION
